Sub-requirement: FR-01.1: The system shall allow users to log in and log out.
Planned check: TC-FR-01.1: Login with valid/invalid credentials; logout makes the old session unusable.

Sub-requirement: FR-01.2: Users shall only view information and perform actions allowed by their permissions.
Planned check: TC-FR-01.2: Run read/write requests as Admin, Engineer, Viewer and unauthenticated caller; verify allowed and denied operations.

Sub-requirement: FR-01.3: Application roles, such as Admin and Viewer, shall be separate from incident responsibilities, such as Commander and Scribe.
Planned check: TC-FR-01.3: Confirm an incident responsibility cannot grant configuration or user-admin access; finalize responsibility representation.

Sub-requirement: FR-02.1: Authorized users shall be able to create an incident with a title, description, affected service, and severity.
Planned check: TC-FR-02.1: Create with all required fields; omit each required field and verify rejection without partial records.

Sub-requirement: FR-02.2: The system shall generate a unique ID, record the reporter and creation time, and set the initial status to OPEN.
Planned check: TC-FR-02.2: Create two incidents; verify distinct IDs, correct creator/time and OPEN status.

Sub-requirement: FR-03.1: The system shall check the source and required fields of incoming alerts and reject invalid requests.
Planned check: TC-FR-03.1: Send valid, missing and invalid signatures and malformed required fields; only valid events are accepted.

Sub-requirement: FR-03.2: Receiving the same event again shall not create another alert or incident.
Planned check: TC-FR-03.2: Replay and concurrently submit one event; one alert/incident persists and the result is reused; changed content conflicts.

Sub-requirement: FR-03.3: A new alert related to an active incident shall be linked to it using configured matching rules.
Planned check: TC-FR-03.3: Send distinct events with matching source/service/key concurrently; one active incident contains both; different keys stay separate.

Sub-requirement: FR-03.4: If no matching incident is found, the system shall create a new incident.
Planned check: TC-FR-03.4: Send a new key, no key, and a recurrence after resolution; each creates the expected new incident.

Sub-requirement: FR-04.1: The system shall support SEV1, SEV2, SEV3, and SEV4.
Planned check: TC-FR-04.1: Accept SEV1 through SEV4 and reject other severity values.

Sub-requirement: FR-04.2: Authorized users shall be able to change severity, with the reason recorded.
Planned check: TC-FR-04.2: Change severity with a reason; verify actor/history and unchanged copied SLA targets; reject missing reason.

Sub-requirement: FR-04.3: The incident board shall allow sorting by severity and time remaining before an SLA deadline.
Planned check: TC-FR-04.3: Sort a fixture board by severity and SLA deadline; verify expected order.

Sub-requirement: FR-05.1: The system shall assign a new incident to the service's on-call responder or configured fallback contact.
Planned check: TC-FR-05.1: Create inside an on-call slot and outside all slots; verify scheduled user and fallback respectively.

Sub-requirement: FR-05.2: Authorized users shall be able to reassign an incident to another person or team.
Planned check: TC-FR-05.2: Reassign to another user and record history; team reassignment is deferred in this plan, so the original statement is only partly covered.

Sub-requirement: FR-05.3: The system shall display the current owner and record who changed the assignment, when, and from whom to whom.
Planned check: TC-FR-05.3: After reassignment or acknowledgement by another user, verify displayed owner and old/new owner, actor and time in history. ACK-OWNER: after escalation notifies B, test A-first and B-first acknowledgement; the winner becomes assignee and the later attempt cannot overwrite it.

Sub-requirement: FR-06.1: The system shall support OPEN, ACKNOWLEDGED, INVESTIGATING, IDENTIFIED, MONITORING, RESOLVED, and CLOSED.
Planned check: TC-FR-06.1: Walk the seven-state lifecycle and verify persisted/displayed statuses.

Sub-requirement: FR-06.2: Only authorized users or configured system actions shall be able to change the status.
Planned check: TC-FR-06.2: Attempt state commands as Viewer and unauthenticated caller; reject without state/history changes.

Sub-requirement: FR-06.3: The system shall allow only approved transitions and record each accepted change with its actor and time.
Planned check: TC-FR-06.3: Exercise each approved transition; verify actor/time and one accepted history entry.

Sub-requirement: FR-06.4: An invalid transition shall be rejected without changing the incident.
Planned check: TC-FR-06.4: Exercise unlisted transitions and a stale version; reject with original state intact.

Sub-requirement: FR-07.1: The system shall notify the assigned responder in the application.
Planned check: TC-FR-07.1: Create an incident; verify its assignee receives one readable in-app notification and another user cannot read it.

Sub-requirement: FR-07.2: Email or a Slack webhook may be added as an external notification channel.
Planned check: TC-FR-07.2: If selected, send one external notification through a stub and verify the configured destination.

Sub-requirement: FR-07.3: If an incident remains unacknowledged at the deadline and another escalation level exists, the system shall notify that level.
Planned check: TC-FR-07.3: Advance time past a deadline; notify the next contact once and keep the existing assignee.

Sub-requirement: FR-07.4: Accepted acknowledgement shall cancel pending acknowledgement escalations.
Planned check: TC-FR-07.4: Acknowledge, then run the poller; no further acknowledgement escalation fires; also test both commit orders in a race.

Sub-requirement: FR-07.5: If the incident remains unacknowledged after all levels are exhausted, the system shall notify the fallback contact and leave it open.
Planned check: TC-FR-07.5: Exhaust all steps without acknowledgement; fallback is notified once, incident remains OPEN, and later acknowledgement still succeeds.

Sub-requirement: FR-07.6: Escalation deadlines shall be stored persistently and re-evaluated after restart.
Planned check: TC-FR-07.6: Restart with an overdue task; process one step once and give the next contact a full waiting period.

Sub-requirement: FR-07.7: Before escalating, the system shall check the stored deadline and current incident record. Only an OPEN incident with no accepted acknowledgement shall be eligible.
Planned check: TC-FR-07.7: Run the poller before due time and after acknowledgement/resolution; no ineligible escalation commits.

Sub-requirement: FR-07.8: Notification attempts, failures, and escalation events shall be recorded.
Planned check: TC-FR-07.8: Verify successful notification/escalation history; induce a persistence failure and verify rollback plus an operational failure log.

Sub-requirement: FR-07.9: If external delivery is included, failures shall be visible for retry.
Planned check: TC-FR-07.9: If an external channel is selected, simulate failure and verify visible retry status without changing incident status.

Sub-requirement: FR-08.1: The system shall keep a timeline of alerts, status changes, assignments, comments, notifications, escalations, and response actions.
Planned check: TC-FR-08.1: Create, alert, assign, comment, escalate and transition; verify the corresponding timeline entries.

Sub-requirement: FR-08.2: Each entry shall identify what happened, when, and who or what performed it.
Planned check: TC-FR-08.2: Check actor/system identity, timestamp and event details on timeline entries.

Sub-requirement: FR-08.3: Corrections shall be added as new entries linked to the original entry. The original shall remain unchanged.
Planned check: TC-FR-08.3: Add an amendment; original text stays unchanged and correction links to it.

Sub-requirement: FR-09.1: Authorized users shall be able to add comments, investigation findings, and updates to an incident.
Planned check: TC-FR-09.1: Post two authorized comments concurrently; both survive and Incident version is unchanged by those inserts. COMMENT-CONCURRENT: repeat while a status change occurs and confirm comments do not cause version conflicts.

Sub-requirement: FR-09.2: These contributions shall remain available in the incident record and follow the incident's access permissions.
Planned check: TC-FR-09.2: Reload comments after restart; authorized readers can view them and unauthorized requests are rejected.

Sub-requirement: FR-10.1: Responders shall be able to record suspected or confirmed causes, resolution steps, and evidence of recovery.
Planned check: TC-FR-10.1: Save investigation findings and a recovery note; verify persistence and require the note before resolution.

Sub-requirement: FR-10.2: An incident may be resolved after recovery is verified even if its root cause is still unknown.
Planned check: TC-FR-10.2: Move INVESTIGATING to MONITORING and RESOLVED with recovery evidence while cause remains unknown.

Sub-requirement: FR-10.3: The system shall allow responders to record corrective and preventive actions.
Planned check: TC-FR-10.3: Create corrective/preventive action items and verify they remain linked to the incident postmortem.

Sub-requirement: FR-11.1: Users shall be able to prepare a postmortem containing the summary, impact, findings, timeline, resolution, and follow-up actions.
Planned check: TC-FR-11.1: Save and reload summary, impact, findings, recovery and follow-up actions; reconcile omitted fields in the short data model.

Sub-requirement: FR-11.2: The incident timeline shall be available while preparing the report.
Planned check: TC-FR-11.2: Open postmortem preparation and verify the incident timeline is available.

Sub-requirement: FR-11.3: Each action item shall have an owner, due date, and completion status.
Planned check: TC-FR-11.3: Create an action item with owner, due date and status; due date must be restored to the short model or explicitly deferred.

Sub-requirement: FR-11.4: The system may generate a draft from the incident timeline.
Planned check: TC-FR-11.4: If selected, generate a timeline-based draft and require human review before saving it as final.

Sub-requirement: FR-12.1: The dashboard shall show total, open, and resolved incidents, severity counts, and average response and resolution times.
Planned check: TC-FR-12.1: Check counts against fixture records; average times are deferred in the short plan and need a scope decision.

Sub-requirement: FR-12.2: Users shall be able to filter by date, severity, status, team, and service, and view each incident's owner and SLA indicators.
Planned check: TC-FR-12.2: Verify service/status/severity filters and owner/SLA display; reconcile date/team filters before claiming full coverage.

Sub-requirement: FR-12.3: Live updates may deliver saved changes without a manual refresh. The dashboard itself is in the initial scope; live updates are an extension.
Planned check: TC-FR-12.3: If selected, save a change in one session and verify the connected board updates without manual refresh.

Sub-requirement: FR-13.1: The system shall record incident changes, permission changes, and changes to service and escalation settings.
Planned check: TC-FR-13.1: Change incident data and Admin configuration; verify incident timeline and configuration audit records.

Sub-requirement: FR-13.2: Each record shall identify the user or system actor, action, time, and affected item.
Planned check: TC-FR-13.2: Check each audit entry contains actor, action, affected item and time.

Sub-requirement: FR-13.3: Existing audit entries shall not be editable through the application.
Planned check: TC-FR-13.3: Attempt audit edits through application endpoints; existing entries cannot be overwritten.

Sub-requirement: FR-14.1: Authorized users shall be able to add and update services, their owners, criticality levels, and response and resolution targets.
Planned check: TC-FR-14.1: Create/update service owner and targets; reconcile service criticality omitted from the short model.

Sub-requirement: FR-14.2: Users may record service dependencies to support investigation.
Planned check: TC-FR-14.2: If selected, save a service dependency and display it as a possible relationship, not proof of shared cause.

Sub-requirement: FR-15.1: Authorized users shall be able to assign responders to on-call time slots using one configured project time zone.
Planned check: TC-FR-15.1: Create adjacent slots, reject overlapping slots, and check selected display zone and boundary interpretation.

Sub-requirement: FR-15.2: The system shall select the responder scheduled at the incident time, or use a configured fallback if no assignment exists.
Planned check: TC-FR-15.2: Create at slot start, just before end, exactly at end and in a gap; verify the correct responder/fallback.

Sub-requirement: FR-15.3: Automatic rotations and temporary schedule overrides may be added.
Planned check: TC-FR-15.3: If selected, test rotation boundaries and override precedence without changing historical assignments.

Sub-requirement: FR-16.1: The system shall maintain separate response and resolution clocks for each incident.
Planned check: TC-FR-16.1: Verify response and resolution values progress independently and are both visible.

Sub-requirement: FR-16.2: Both clocks shall start at incident creation. The response clock shall stop at the first accepted acknowledgement; the resolution clock shall stop at accepted resolution.
Planned check: TC-FR-16.2: Use a controlled clock; acknowledgement stops only response, resolution stops resolution, and both start at creation.

Sub-requirement: FR-16.3: The system shall calculate deadlines from the service targets and incident severity, display remaining time, and indicate breaches.
Planned check: TC-FR-16.3: Verify fixed copied targets, remaining time and exact-deadline/beyond-deadline behavior; severity edits do not reset clocks.

Sub-requirement: FR-16.4: The initial version shall count elapsed time continuously.
Planned check: TC-FR-16.4: Advance through night and weekend; all elapsed time counts.

Sub-requirement: FR-16.5: SLA pauses and business-hours calendars may be added after their rules are agreed.
Planned check: TC-FR-16.5: If selected later, test agreed pause/calendar rules; no such rules are implemented in the initial plan.

Sub-requirement: FR-17.1: Responders shall be able to search previous incidents using keywords and filter by service or severity.
Planned check: TC-FR-17.1: Search keywords and service; reconcile the older severity filter omitted from the short search description.

Sub-requirement: FR-17.2: Results shall provide access to previous findings, fixes, and postmortems that the user is allowed to view.
Planned check: TC-FR-17.2: Open a search result and read permitted findings, fix and postmortem.

Sub-requirement: FR-18.1: If included, local AI shall suggest investigation steps using the incident details and available previous records.
Planned check: TC-FR-18.1: If selected, provide bounded prior-incident fixtures to local AI and verify a structured investigation suggestion.

Sub-requirement: FR-18.2: Suggestions shall be labelled as AI-generated and identify the records used.
Planned check: TC-FR-18.2: If selected, show AI label and referenced incident IDs; reject references absent from provided context.

Sub-requirement: FR-18.3: Log and deployment analysis may be added when those data sources are available.
Planned check: TC-FR-18.3: If selected later, test log/deployment retrieval against bounded fixtures.

Sub-requirement: FR-18.4: Users shall be able to continue manually when AI is unavailable.
Planned check: TC-FR-18.4: If selected, timeout/fail AI and verify manual search and incident commands still work.

Sub-requirement: FR-19.1: If AI suggestions are included, an authorized responder shall review them before acting. This control is required whenever that feature is included.
Planned check: TC-FR-19.1: If selected, show suggestions for review; any chosen state change still uses normal authorized controls.

Sub-requirement: FR-19.2: The system shall record whether a suggested action was accepted or rejected.
Planned check: TC-FR-19.2: If AI is selected, settle how acceptance/rejection is stored, then verify both choices are attributed and persisted.

Sub-requirement: FR-19.3: The system shall not automatically execute remediation.
Planned check: TC-FR-19.3: Review endpoints and tools and try an AI command-like output; no automatic remediation is executed.

Sub-requirement: FR-20.1: If included, the system shall store deployment details and allow users to link incidents to deployments.
Planned check: TC-FR-20.1: If selected later, record a deployment and link an incident using valid IDs.

Sub-requirement: FR-20.2: Reports may include Deployment Frequency, Lead Time for Changes, Change Failure Rate, and Mean Time to Restore using agreed definitions and available data.
Planned check: TC-FR-20.2: If selected later, calculate each agreed DORA metric from known fixture inputs.

Sub-requirement: FR-20.3: Missing input data shall be shown as unavailable rather than reported as zero.
Planned check: TC-FR-20.3: If selected later, remove metric inputs and verify unavailable is displayed rather than zero.

Sub-requirement: FR-21.1: If included, customer-facing updates shall be separate from internal incident notes.
Planned check: TC-FR-21.1: If selected later, verify a public update excludes internal-only incident notes.

Sub-requirement: FR-21.2: Only authorized users shall approve and publish external updates.
Planned check: TC-FR-21.2: If selected later, reject publication by an unauthorized user and record authorized approval.

Sub-requirement: FR-22.1: If included, the system shall check configured service endpoints and raise an alert after a configured failure threshold.
Planned check: TC-FR-22.1: If selected, simulate the configured number of failed checks and verify a deduplicated alert.

Sub-requirement: FR-22.2: Recovery shall update the matching alert.
Planned check: TC-FR-22.2: If selected, simulate recovery and update the matching alert without automatically resolving the incident.

Sub-requirement: FR-22.3: Automatic incident resolution shall require an explicit recovery rule.
Planned check: TC-FR-22.3: Initial version: health-check recovery must not auto-resolve an incident; any future auto-resolution requires a separately approved rule.
